entities.evidence: Seir names the hill country inhabited by the Horites.
אֵיל begins the place-name אֵיל פָּארָן, the landmark reached in the campaign.
פָּארָן completes the name of the landmark that the relative clause locates by the wilderness.

review.translation: [and|0] [the Horites|1] [in their hill country of|2] [Seir|3] [as far as|4] [El|5] [Paran|6], [which|7] {is} [by|8] [the wilderness|9].

draft.change: Add Genesis 14:6 as evidence for the existing definite-object sense of the Hebrew particle.
draft.definition: אֵת introduces the definite person or thing a verb acts on.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:5–6 lists the peoples the kings struck. וְאֶת הַחֹרִי continues the same construction across the verse boundary.

analysis.evidence: וְאֶת הַחֹרִי adds the Horites to the peoples whom the kings struck. The governing verb is וַיַּכּוּ, “they struck,” in Genesis 14:5, and the article הַ makes הַחֹרִי definite.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and.” אֶת is the unsuffixed direct-object particle.

analysis.evidence: וְאֶת marks הַחֹרִי as another object of the preceding verb of striking. The plural suffix in בְּהַרְרָם, “in their hill country,” identifies the Horites collectively as the people living in Seir.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine singular absolute gentilic used as a noun. The singular refers collectively to the people.

analysis.evidence: שֵׂעִיר names the Horites’ hill country, and עַד אֵיל פָּארָן traces the campaign as far as El-paran. The geographic setting supports the regional sense of הַר.
analysis.morphology: The locative preposition בְּ precedes a masculine singular construct noun with a third-person masculine plural possessive suffix referring to the Horites.

draft.change: Add a geographical entry for שֵׂעִיר. The existing שׂער article explicitly sets this proper name apart, and the verse supplies no derivation from the word for hair.
draft.definition: Seir, the hill country inhabited by the Horites and later by Esau.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:6 names Seir as the Horites’ hill country. Deuteronomy 2:12 recalls that the Horites formerly lived in Seir, and Genesis 36:8 says that Esau settled in Mount Seir.

analysis.evidence: בְּהַרְרָם שֵׂעִיר names the Horites’ hill country as Seir. The following עַד אֵיל פָּארָן, “as far as El-paran,” gives the extent of the attackers’ advance.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun naming a place, with no prefix or suffix. It stands in apposition to בְּהַרְרָם, “in their hill country.”
analysis.sense: The hill country of Seir where the Horites lived.

analysis.evidence: In עַד אֵיל פָּארָן, עַד introduces El-paran as the geographic limit reached in the campaign against the Horites.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: as far as, up to, to (a place or person)

analysis.evidence: עַד אֵיל פָּארָן marks the endpoint of the route, “as far as the terebinth of Paran.” The clause אֲשֶׁר עַל הַמִּדְבָּר locates that landmark at the edge of the wilderness. The source’s proper-name tag fits the full place-name אֵיל פָּארָן, while the marked word supplies its tree element.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state. אֵיל is the construct form of אַיִל, with פָּארָן as its complement.
analysis.sense: A great tree or terebinth that gives a location its name.

draft.change: Add a geographic entry for פָּארָן under its own consonants, פארנ. Its verbal derivation is unknown.
draft.definition: Paran is a geographic name used for a wilderness and in the name El-paran.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:6 locates El-paran beside the wilderness. Genesis 21:21 names the wilderness of Paran as Ishmael’s dwelling place.

analysis.evidence: עַד אֵיל פָּארָן means “as far as El-paran,” marking the extent of the advance. The clause אֲשֶׁר עַל הַמִּדְבָּר locates that landmark beside the wilderness. Genesis 21:21 independently uses פָּארָן in מִדְבַּר פָּארָן, “the wilderness of Paran.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. It is the second element of the place-name אֵיל פָּארָן.
analysis.sense: Paran, the region named in the landmark El-paran.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause describing אֵיל פָּארָן. The phrase עַל הַמִּדְבָּר supplies the predicate, yielding “which is by the wilderness.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew relative particle without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The relative clause אֲשֶׁר עַל הַמִּדְבָּר locates El-paran beside the wilderness. The wilderness serves as a landmark.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר עַל הַמִּדְבָּר locates El-paran beside the wilderness. El-paran is the named place, and הַמִּדְבָּר describes the adjoining terrain.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial מ of the masculine singular noun in the absolute state.
